\vspace{2pt}
\parbox{\textwidth}{\justifying\scriptsize *Locked reference: size (Ref.) and source of each real dataset or task. The rows that remain once the reference is set aside form the eligible training pool, from which every trial draws its training rows. Groups. (A): the $11$ new binary datasets. (C): the $12$ clinical tasks. (D): the $39$ supporting datasets, namely the $34$ binary confirmation datasets (including the $18$ development datasets, marked (dev), on which the gate and the candidate space were frozen) and the $5$ multiclass datasets. (E): the $14$ datasets of the OpenML collection, with names shortened and identified by the OpenML ID. Setting (B), the synthetic population, is generated rather than drawn from a dataset and is described in this appendix. Min.: minority-class share; for a multiclass dataset, the smallest class. Split: $2{,}430$ training rows by default (SEARCH $630$, POOL $1{,}800$); $^{\dagger}$: $1{,}000$ training rows (SEARCH $259$, POOL $741$). Trials per task: $100$ in (A), (D), and binary (E); $200$ in (C); $60$ in multiclass (D) and (E). Domains briefly characterize the public sources, and exact definitions live in the code-repository loaders. The $28$ domain labels map to seven groups, all represented among the $64$ real datasets: Health (Healthcare, Medical, Radiology, Clinical, Survey, Public Health, ICU); Finance, banking and insurance (Finance, Banking, Insurance, Crowdfund); Agriculture and mining (Agriculture, Mining); Cyber and software (Software, Cyber); Commerce, services and HR (E-commerce, Marketing, HR, Employment, Automotive); Social, legal and media (Social, Justice, Media, Gaming); Science and vision (Physics, Biology, Vision, Speech).}
